summary: John Whaley Watson was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Bombay Staff Corps (~1861–1889), as President of the Rajasthik Court in Kathiawar (~1873–1889), and as political agent at the Kathiawar Agency (1881–1889).

John William Neill worked in Indology after studying at King's College London and the University of Edinburgh. He was a Fellow at the University of Calcutta (1883), Professor at University College London (1896–1917), and Reader at SOAS.

John Wilson, an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (1835) and Cave Temple Commission (1848–1861), and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1868).
John Zephaniah Holwell was an Indology scholar who studied surgery at Guy's Hospital from ~1727 to 1732. In 1767, he became a Fellow of the Royal Society.

Join Saeki worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Jōchō Chihaya and at Sennyu-ji. He served at Kangakuin, as head (管主) of Horyuji Kangakuin (1903–1950), and taught at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1927).
Joji Fujii is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1966 to 1976 and later held a post there from ~1985 to 2011.

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950) and Kyoto University. He later held posts at Shuchiin University and as a professor at Otemae University (~1966–1994).

Jon Holt is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a Ph.D. at the University of Washington, later becoming Professor of Japanese at Portland State University in 2010.

Jon Kabat-Zinn works in religious studies, earning a Ph.D. from MIT (~1964–1971). He founded and led the Stress Reduction Clinic (~1979–1995) and became Professor of Medicine Emeritus at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School.

Jon Skarpeid works in Buddhist studies and linguistics. His appointments include Associate Professor at the University of Stavanger (attested 2017), head and Pali lecturer at Shan State Buddhist University (attested 2019), and a post at Leiden University (attested 2019).

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU (2013–2020), and as Distinguished Professor at the University of Toronto (~2020).

Jonas Buchholz is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He has held affiliations with Heidelberg University (attested 2021), the University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne (attested 2023), and The Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation (attested 2025).

Jonathan A. Silk is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, and has held posts at Yale (1998–2002), the University of California, and Leiden University (2007).

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2003), later holding posts at Drew University and Princeton University (from 2008).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral work at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1974–1984) and taught as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Duquette is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his Ph.D. from Université de Montréal. He held posts at Kyoto University, the University of Oxford (2015–2019), the University of Cambridge (2019), and the University of Birmingham (2020–2021).

Jonathan Edelmann is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford by 2009 and became an Assistant Professor at the University of Florida in 2015.

Jonathan Geen is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001, and went on to teach at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Oxford's Corpus Christi College. He served as a fellow and tutor at New College (~1967–2000), taught at King's College London (~2000–2013), and is a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford.

Jonathan Lear was a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University. He taught at Yale (1978–1996), Cambridge (1979–1985), and served as a Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago (2014–2022).
